colonyCapture.source: Globulation2/glob2 master at 9598555f (Globulation2/glob2#1868, which adds GLOB2_PRESENTED_CAPTURE, GLOB2_COLONY_STATUS and a fixed 40 ms presentation step to tools/MenuColonyHarness.cpp record-colony), dev build; not a released package.
colonyCapture.renderer: Active SDL GPU backend (GLOB2_RENDERER=sdl-gpu), 1470x828 logical window at 2x pixel density, 2940x1656 presented-frame readback; high-resolution artwork resolved by the default Auto setting on Apple silicon (terrain tile=64).

graphicsQualification.method: Side-by-side crop of the same map region at native 2940x1656 against the superseded release capture: identical camera position and matching high-resolution sprite and terrain detail.
graphicsQualification.limits: No settings-screen proof; Auto, not an explicit High resolution choice. Source build, not a release binary.

hero.scene: Live menu-colony simulation drawn by MenuColony::draw with status bars, no menu UI and no crop. Camera is the menu's own: colony centre at two-thirds of the width.
hero.recording: 550 lossless BMP frames; simulation and presentation clock both advance 40 ms per frame (25 fps real time)
hero.loop: 15 seconds: source 4-18 seconds followed by a one-second dissolve from 18-19 into 3-4. Opening and closing meet at source 4. No speed change.
hero.encode: libx264 High, preset slow, CRF 23, yuv420p, faststart, Lanczos scale
hero.poster: Exact decoded first delivered frame, cwebp -q 90, 1600/960 wide
hero.limits: Genuine menu background, not human play. Early frames (under about 1.6 s) show coarse terrain while it builds; they are outside the selected range. No outside/generated imagery, repaint, recolor or reconstructed game state.
hero.speedCheck: Cloud-shadow brightness drift over 10 s of the same sea region: 1.08 luminance/s, against 0.79 for the real-time 0.11.6.1 release capture and 2.79 for the superseded capture.

supersededColonyCaptures.reason: Water, shorelines and clouds advanced by each frame's wall-clock capture time, so they played about 3.5 times too fast (cloud-shadow drift 2.79 against 0.79 luminance/s for the real-time release capture). Superseded by a capture whose presentation clock advances 40 ms per recorded frame.
